title: Condensate Pipe Flood Test
source: spec/Condensate_Pipe_Flood_Test.html (9 July 2012, Rev 1) — the sanitary flood-test sheet retitled for ACMV condensate drain runs: same rows, same sign-off block, same footer revision. Filed under ACMV because condensate pipework is tested by that trade, and kept as its own template rather than a variant of SPF so the printed title matches the paper form the consultant accepts. The supplied file was saved with a completed record in it (client, From/To, dates); those are record values, not template values, and are not carried here.

sections.title: Flood Test Readings
sections._note:
`page_break_before` on the opening section is what keeps this on one sheet: `paginate` gives every section its own page unless at least one declares a break, and a break on the first section is a no-op for layout — it is already page 1. Same idiom as `fcu-lcp-checklist.json` and `chemical-flush-checklist.json`. Without it this record printed 3 pages, the second carrying nothing but the Remarks box.

Item numbers follow the paper form, which starts at 2 — items From / To are the unnumbered rows above, carried here as header fields. The source prints Date and Time in one row (items 3 and 5); a checklist row carries a single control, so each is split into a dated row and a timed continuation row rather than adding form-specific rendering (Hard Rule #4). Design Pressure and the two pressure readings are text, not number: the paper form is filled with words as often as figures ("NA", "Refer to attached test photo").

rows._note: Photos attach here because the paper form's own reading is routinely "Refer to attached test photo". The print row appears only when photos exist, so a record without them matches the source page.

sections.title: Remarks
sections._note: Two fields because the paper form carries two: a free Remarks box and the ruled REMARKS / INSTRUMENTS USED line beneath it. The instruments line stays free text — the source form does not tabulate calibrated instruments the way the Power Turn-on form does, so no `instruments` block is declared.

sections.title: Sign-off
sections._note: An in-flow `sign_off` section rather than the top-level `footer`: PrintView always gives the footer a page of its own, and the source form closes the single sheet with the signature rows directly beneath the remarks. Both carry the same slots through `collectSignatureSlots`, so the status workflow is unchanged. Same idiom as `ductwork-air-leakage-test.json`. No `page_break_before` — it shares the page.
